title: Exercise: Conveyor Jam Detection
oneLiner: Stop a conveyor and latch a jam alarm when a photo-eye stays blocked too long while the belt runs, with a reset that only works once the jam is cleared and no automatic restart.
keyTakeaway: Time Motor AND PhotoEye with a TON, latch the jam, clear it only when the eye is clear and Reset is pressed, and put NOT Jam into the seal-in so the motor needs a fresh Start.
explanation:
On a conveyor, a part that stops moving piles up the parts behind it. A common, cheap way to detect that is a timeout: if the photo-eye stays blocked much longer than a part normally takes to pass, assume a jam, stop the belt and tell the operator.

This exercise adds that to the start/stop seal-in, with a reset that only works once the jam has been cleared, and without restarting the belt by itself afterwards.
